page.name: Shipping and delivery updates
page.h1: Send shipping and delivery updates when the state changes
page.metaTitle: Shipping and delivery updates, in real time
page.metaDescription: Dispatch notices, tracking updates and delivery windows sent as they happen, paced per number and logged for the record.
page.lede: Dispatch notices, tracking updates and delivery windows go out when the state actually changes, not on a timer. On the SMS channel the platform spreads a dispatch batch to the limit your provider applies per number, so a whole route does not stall halfway through.

sections.h: The four updates a customer waits for
bullets: In transit or delayed, when the status genuinely changes
Out for delivery, on the day it matters
Delivered, or a failed attempt with a next step
p: Send on real state changes, not on a timer. An update that says nothing new trains the recipient to ignore the next one — and a delivery-window message that arrives late is worse than none.

sections.h: Batches that drain instead of stalling
p: A dispatch batch can exceed what one number absorbs. On the SMS channel the platform paces the batch to the per-number limit and can route to another connected account if one stops accepting traffic, so a failed provider does not silently strand half a route.
bullets: Batches spread to the provider limit per sender number
Automatic failover between connected SMS accounts
Receipts normalized so a rejection is distinguishable from silence

p: The accuracy of the tracking data, the decision to notify, and any rules about contacting recipients are yours. The platform carries the message on your account and reports what happened to it.

faq.q: Can we hold updates until a window opens?
faq.a: Scheduled and bulk sending are console features. For delivery updates, though, sending when the state changes is usually the better pattern.

faq.q: Will a delayed provider break the whole batch?
faq.a: On the SMS channel, traffic can route to another connected account. That keeps the batch moving; it does not guarantee the destination network accepts every message.

faq.q: Do we get told which notices failed?
faq.a: Each send carries a status, and failures record the provider’s reason where one was returned. That is the record support works from.
